title: Microsoft Teams: external presenters in event group chat
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's rollout notice and roadmap targets, and the documented admin paths and PowerShell calls are supported. It distinguishes existing external-access and event-verification controls from the undocumented chat-specific switch, and leaves change-specific licensing and tenantId compliance effects open.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support presenters from outside the hosting tenant in event group chat.
claims.quote: This change enables presenters who are outside the tenant hosting the meeting or event to participate in the event group chat.

claims.claim: Event group chat is the private coordination chat for organizers, co-organizers and presenters during an event or structured meeting.
claims.quote: Event group chat, the private chat for organizers, co-organizers, and presenters in an event or structured meeting, will support external presenters.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn describes event group chat as available before, during and after an event.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

claims.claim: Event group chat is separate from attendee chat.
claims.quote: The event group chat is available before, during, and after an event, and is a separate experience from the chat with attendees.

claims.claim: The capability arrives for its intended users without a new admin enablement step, subject to the stated green-room and existing external-collaboration prerequisites.
claims.quote:
External presenters will be able to join the event group chat used for coordination during a meeting or event.
If your organization wants external presenters to use event group chat, ensure external user collaboration is enabled in Teams admin center > External collaboration.

claims.claim: Both the organization setting and a user policy must allow external access for a user to use it.

claims.claim: The organization settings and user policies for external access are turned on by default.
claims.quote: Both the organization settings and user policies are turned on by default.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTenantFederationConfiguration -AllowFederatedUsers $true to enable tenant federation, subject to the other federation settings.
claims.quote: When set to True (the default value) users will be potentially allowed to communicate with users from other domains.

claims.quote:
The External Collaboration section in the Teams Admin Center (TAC) left rail provides a unified location to manage all external collaboration settings.
External access: This is the existing page to manage configuration of federation and communication with external domains

claims.quote:
In the Teams admin center, go to Users > External access.
Select the Policies tab.
In the list of policies, select the Org-wide default settings.

claims.claim: Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess $true is a documented command for enabling federation in an external-access policy.
claims.quote: Set-CsExternalAccessPolicy -EnableFederationAccess $True

claims.claim: The existing default external-access policy is labeled Org-wide default settings.
claims.quote: In the list of policies, select the Org-wide default settings.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Presenter join verification is configured at Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Verify external presenters before joining an event.
claims.quote:
go to Meetings > Events policies.
Select an existing policy or create a new one.
In the Verify external presenters before joining an event dropdown list, select Yes verify accounts or No verification needed.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP requires external presenters to verify their identity before joining events created by organizers with that policy.
claims.quote:
To require external presenters to verify their identity before joining events created by organizers with this policy, run the following command:
Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalPresenterJoinVerification EOTP

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document presenter join verification as a control over event group chat access.
claims.quote: Searched: "event group chat" "verification". Opened events-external-presenter-join-verification, manage-event-chat and plan-events; verification is documented for joining events, not separately for entering their group chat.

claims.claim: The general Teams retention documentation says messages for an external user joining with another Microsoft 365 organization's account are stored in that user's mailbox in another tenant.
claims.quote: If an external user joins by using an account from another Microsoft 365 organization, your retention policies can't delete messages for this user because they're stored in that user's mailbox in another tenant.
